rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He” is Gabriel, located at the highest horizon, glossed as the sunrise point.
rows.anchor: اى جبريل عليه السلام ﴿ بالأفق الأعلى ﴾ مطلع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns both worlds and rules over them, granting prophethood and intercession to whom He wills and approves, not to whoever merely wishes.
rows.anchor: اى هو مالكهما وله الحكم فيهما يعطى النبوة وشافعة من شاء وارتضى لا من تمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who” is an appositive, or nominative as a phrase of praise: “they are those who.”
rows.anchor: بدل أوفى موضع رفع على المدح اى هم الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major sins are the grave members of the genus of sin, which includes both major and minor sins; they are sins whose punishment is great.
rows.anchor: اى الكبائر من الاثم لان الاثم جنس يشتمل على كبائرر وصغائر والكبائر لاذنوب التى يكبر عقابها

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Hamza and ʿAlī read the phrase in the singular, “the major kind of sin.”
rows.anchor: كبير حمزة وعلى اى النوع الكبير منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawāḥish are more heinous than major sins and are a particular subset of them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والفواحش ﴾ افحس من الكبائر انه قال والفواحش منها خاصة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported distinction calls major sins those threatened with Hellfire and fawāḥish those for which a legal ḥadd is prescribed.
rows.anchor: قيل الكبائر ما اوعد الله عليه النار والفواحس ما شرع فيها الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-lamam means minor sins; the exception is disconnected because minor sins are not part of major sins or fawāḥish.
rows.anchor: اى الصغائر والاستثناء منقطع لانه ليس من اكبائر والفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of al-lamam include a glance, a remark, a touch, and a gesture.
rows.anchor: وهو كالنظرة والقيلة واللمسة والغمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgiveness is vast: He forgives whatever sins He wills even without repentance.
rows.anchor: فيغفر ما شاء من الذنوب من غي توبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew people when He created their father Adam from earth and when they were embryos in their mothers, before they emerged from Adam's loins or their mothers' wombs.
rows.anchor: قبل ان يخرجكم من صلب آدم عليه السلام وقبل ان تخرجوا منبطون امهاتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not claim purity of deeds, abundant good works, or freedom from sins, and do not praise yourselves; humble yourselves, since God knew the pure and pious before you existed.
rows.anchor: فلا تنسبوها إلى زكاء العمل وزيادة الخير والطاعات أو إلى الزكاة والطهارة من المعاصى ولا تثنوا عليها واهضموها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about people who performed good deeds and then boasted, “our prayers, fasting, and pilgrimage.”
rows.anchor: وقيل كان نهاس يعملون اعمالا حسنة ثم يقولون صلاتنا وصيامنا وحجنا فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-praise is forbidden when it expresses vanity or ostentation; mentioning obedience is allowed as gratitude, since rejoicing in obedience is itself obedience.
rows.anchor: وهذا اذا كان على سبيل الاعجاب أو الرياء لاعلى سبيل الاعتراف بالنعمة فانه جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Let God's knowledge suffice instead of people's knowledge, and His reward instead of their praise.
rows.anchor: فاكتفوا بعلمه عن علم الناس وبجزائه عن ثناء الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is mentioned in the scrolls of Abraham; the following description concerns him.
rows.anchor: اى وفى صحف إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waffā means he fulfilled or completed, as in the statement that God completed Abraham's tests; the wording broadly covers every kind of fulfillment.
rows.anchor: اى وفر واتم كقوله فاتمهن واطلاقه ليتناول كل وفاء وتوفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lightened form of the verb is also read; the doubled form emphasizes complete fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وقرىء مخففا والتشديد مبالغة في الوفاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Abraham fulfilled every command God gave him.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ما أمره الله بشىء الا وفى به

rows.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib reports that Abraham pledged never to ask a created being for anything; when cast into the fire, he told Gabriel he had no need of him.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء بن السائب عهد ان لا يسأل مخلوقا فلما قذف في النار قال له جبريل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said Abraham fulfilled his daily practice with four rakʿas at the start of the day, the ḍuḥā prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وفى عمله كل يوم باربع ركعات في صدر النهار وهى صلاة الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Abraham would recite the evening and morning glorification verses at those times; it explains why God called him the one who fulfilled.
rows.anchor: وروى الا اخبركم لم سمى الله خليله الذى وفى كان يقول اذا اصبح واذا امسى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled the thirty portions of Islam: ten in al-Tawba, ten in al-Aḥzāb, and ten in al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: وقيل وفي سهام الاسلام وهى ثلاثون عشرة في التوبة التائبون وعشرة في الاحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul bears another soul's sin; w-z-r means to incur a burden of sin, that is, wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: تز من وزر يزر اذا اكتسب وزرا وهو الاثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An” is lightened from the emphatic particle, with an implicit pronoun of the matter; the clause is genitive as a substitute for “in the scrolls of Moses,” or nominative as the predicate of “it is.”
rows.anchor: والضمير ضمير الشان ومحل ان وما بعدهاالجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is requited for his striving; Arabic may make the deed a direct object by omitting the preposition.
rows.anchor: ثم يجزى العبد سعيه يقال جزاءه الله عمله وجزاه على عمله بحذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun can refer to the recompense, which is then explained by “the fullest recompense,” or the latter phrase can be an apposition.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون الضمير للجزاء ثم فسره بقوله ﴿ الجزاء الأوفى ﴾ أو ابدله عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation is that God causes fathers to die and brings sons to life.
rows.anchor: قيل أمت الآباء وأحيا الابناء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that He causes death through disbelief and gives life through faith.
rows.anchor: أو أمات بالكفر واحيا بالايمان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that He causes death in this world and gives life in the next.
rows.anchor: أو امت هنا واحيا ثمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later creation is resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: الاحياء بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Everything” is accusative as the object of an implicit verb explained by the following “We created”; the nominative reading is anomalous.
rows.anchor: كل منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر وقرى بالرفع شاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the accusative: with the nominative, “We created it” could modify “thing,” leaving “by measure” as predicate, or itself be the predicate.
rows.anchor: والنصب اول لانه لو رفع لامكن ان يكون خلقناه في موضع الجر وصفا لشىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative construction makes creation general to every thing, which is the verse's intended meaning; “We created” cannot be an adjective of “thing” because it explains the verb that governs it.
rows.anchor: فيكون الخلق عاما لكل شىء وهو المراد بالاية ولا يجوز في النصب ان يكون خلقناه صفة لشىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-qadar can mean according to a prior decree, or that each thing is created precisely, in an ordered way that accords with wisdom.
rows.anchor: والقدر والقدر التقدير اى بتقدير سابق أو خلقنا كل شىء مقدرا محكما مرتبا على تحسب ما اقتضته الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, every thing was measured and recorded in the Preserved Tablet, with its state and time known before it came to be.
rows.anchor: أو مقدرا مكتوبا في اللوح معلوما قبل كونه قد علما حاله ومانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse continues the point that God's command is a single act, swift as a blink of an eye.
rows.anchor: وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة جاء مشركوا قريش إلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر فنزلت الاية

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar used to swear that the verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر يحلف انها نزلت في القدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All who are upon it” means everyone on earth, who will perish.
rows.anchor: على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Face of your Lord” means His essence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويبقى وجه ربك ﴾ ذاته ﴿ ذو الجلال ﴾ ذو العظمة والسلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-jalāl means possessing majesty and sovereignty; it grammatically describes the Face.
rows.anchor: ذو العظمة والسلطان وهو صفة الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ikrām means pardon and beneficence; this is one of God's mighty attributes.
rows.anchor: بالتجاوز والاحسان وهذه الصفة من عظيم صفات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith urges persistent invocation with the words “O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.”
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث الظوا بباذا الجلال ولاكرام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet passed a man praying and saying this invocation, and told him that his prayer had been answered.
rows.anchor: وروى انه عليه السلام مر بجل وهو يصلى ويقول باذا الجلال والاكرام فقال قد استجيب لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are two gardens below the two gardens promised to those brought near, for those of the right.
rows.anchor: ومن دون تبينك الجنتين الموعودتين للمقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two gardens are black-green from the intensity of their greenness.
rows.anchor: سوداوان من شدة الخضرة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says dahma means blackness.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل الدهمة السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūrūn means that you kindle the fire and draw it from the firesticks.
rows.anchor: تقدحونها وتستخرجونها من الزناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs make fire by rubbing two sticks: the upper is the male firestick and the lower the female, likened to a stallion and its mate.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقدح بعودين تحك احداهما على الآخر ويسمون الأعلى الزند والاسفل الزندة شبهوهما بالفحل والطروقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire reminds people of Hell: God made livelihood depend on it so everyone needs it, sees it, and recalls the threatened punishment.
rows.anchor: تذكير النار جهنم حيث علقنا بها أسباب المعاش عممنا بالحاجة اليها البلوى لتكون حاضرة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire is a benefit for travelers lodging in desert country, or for people whose stomachs or provisions are empty; aqwat al-dār means a house became empty.
rows.anchor: للمسافرين النازلين في القواء وهي القفر أو الذين خلت بطونهم أو مزاودهم من الطعام من قولهم أقوت الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from human creation to grain that sustains life, then water used with food, then fire for baking; food depends on these three, indispensable while the body lives.
rows.anchor: بدأ بذكر خلق الانسان فقال أفرأيتم ما تمنون لأن النعمة فيه سابقة على جميع النعم ثم بما به قوامه وهو الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day” is accusative as governed by “humiliating,” or by an omitted “remember,” magnifying that day.
rows.anchor: منصوب بمهين أو باضمارا ذكر تعظيما لليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God resurrects all of them, leaving no one unraised, or brings them together in the same state.
rows.anchor: كلهم لا يترك منهم أحد غير مبعوث أو مجتمعين في حال واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God informs them to shame, rebuke, and expose them publicly; overwhelmed with disgrace before witnesses, they wish to be rushed to Hell.
rows.anchor: تخجيلا لهم وتوبيخا وتشهيرا بحالهم يتمنون عنده المسارعة بهم إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompassed their deeds by counting them, missing nothing.
rows.anchor: احاط به عددا لم يفته منه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forgot their deeds because they were careless about them when committing them; people remember only matters they regard as important.
rows.anchor: لانهم تهاونوا ونوابه حين ارتكبوه وانما تحفظ معظمات الامور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God witnesses everything; nothing is absent from Him.
rows.anchor: لا يغيب عن شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with “the Emigrants”; it refers to the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: معطوف على المهاجرين وهم الانصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They settled in Medina.
rows.anchor: توطنوا المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that they sincerely embraced faith, with ellipsis as in the poetic phrase “I fed her straw and cold water.”
rows.anchor: وأخلصوا الايمان كقوله علفتها تبنا وماء باردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they made faith a settled home, being firmly established and steadfast in it as they were settled in Medina.
rows.anchor: أو وجعلوا الايمان مستقرا ومتوطنا لهم لتمكنهم واستقامتهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “the abode” means the Abode of Emigration, with the definite article standing for a possessive phrase and “settled” elided before “faith.”
rows.anchor: أو أراد دار الهجرة فاقام لام التعريف في الدار مقام المضاف اليه وحذف تبوئ دار الهجرة والايمان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported interpretation takes “before them” as before the Emigrants' migration.
rows.anchor: وقيل من قبل المهاجرين هجرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār loved the Emigrants so much that they shared their wealth and homes; a man with two wives even gave one up for an Emigrant to marry.
rows.anchor: حتى شاطروهم أموالهم وأنزلوهم منازلهم ونزل من كانت له امرأتان عن احداهما حتى تزوج بها رجل من المهاجرين

words: ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not covet what the Emigrants received from the spoils or elsewhere: their souls neither pursued nor desired any of it as something they needed.
rows.anchor: يعني ان نفوسهم لم تتبع ما أعطوا ولم تطمح إلى شيء منه تحتاج اليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view glosses “need” as envy of the spoils allotted to the Emigrants.
rows.anchor: وقيل حاجة حسدا مما أعطي المهاجرون من الفيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands distress over what they themselves missed, with two possessive phrases elided.
rows.anchor: وقيل 4 لا يجدون في صدورهم من حاجة من فقد ما أوتوا فحذف المضافان

words: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They put others before themselves even when poor; the clause describes their state, supposing their poverty.
rows.anchor: فقر وأصلها خصاص البيت وهى فروجه والجملة في موضع الحال أي مفروضة خصاصتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report tells of an Anṣārī host putting his children to sleep, serving a guest, and extinguishing the lamp so the guest could eat while he went without.
rows.anchor: روى أنه نزل برجل منهم ضيف فنوم الصبية وقرب الطعام وأطفأ المصباح ليشبع ضيفه

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that a roasted head passed among nine needy people, each sending it to a neighbor, until it returned to the first.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس أهدى لبعضهم رأس مشوي وهو مجهود فوجهه إلى جاره فتداولته تسعة أنفس

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd contrasts a youth from Balkh: their asceticism is to endure lack and give others preference when they have food, unlike merely eating when they find it.
rows.anchor: أبو زيد قال لي شاب من أهل بلخ با الزهد عندكم قلت إذا وجدنا أكلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuḥ is a miserly, tight-fisted self eager to withhold; those protected from it attain what they seek.
rows.anchor: والشح أكل اللؤم وأن تكون نفس الرجل كزة حريصه على المنع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another distinction says shuḥ is wrongful consumption of a brother's wealth, while bukhl is withholding one's own.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشح أكل مال أخيك ظلما والبخل منع مالك

rows.speaker: كسرى
rows.claim: Kisrā says avarice is worse than poverty: the poor can recover when wealth comes, unlike the miser.
rows.anchor: وعن كسرى الشح أضر من الفقر لآن الفقير يتسع إذا وجد بخلاف الشحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khāliq is the One who determines what He brings into existence.
rows.anchor: المقدر لما يوجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bāriʾ is the One who brings things into existence.
rows.anchor: الموجد ﴿ المصور ﴾ في الارحام ﴿ له الأسماء الحسنى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muṣawwir shapes creatures in the wombs.
rows.anchor: في الارحام ﴿ له الأسماء الحسنى ﴾ الدالة على الصفات العلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beautiful names indicate God's sublime attributes.
rows.anchor: الدالة على الصفات العلا

words: يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra closes with the theme with which it began.
rows.anchor: ختم السورة بما بدأ به

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra says he asked the Messenger about God's greatest name; the Prophet directed him to the end of al-Ḥashr and told him to recite it often.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه سألت حبيبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الاسم الاعظم فقال عليك بآخر الحشر فأكثر قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent an unlettered man among an unlettered people; “from them” can also mean from their own people, whose lineage and circumstances he knew.
rows.anchor: أي بعث رجلا أميا في قوم أميين وقيل منهم كقوله من انفسكم يعلمون نسبه وأحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Unlettered” derives from the Arab nation, who did not write or read as other nations did.
rows.anchor: والأمي منسوب إلى أمة العرب لأنهم كانوا لا يكتبون ولا يقرؤون من بين الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing began in al-Ṭāʾif; its people learned it from the people of al-Ḥīra, who learned it from the people of al-Anbār.
rows.anchor: وقيل بدئت الكتابة بالطائف وهم أخذوها من ا هل ال حيرة وأهل الحيرة من اهل الأنبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses he recites are the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: يتلو عليهم آياته ﴾ القرآن ﴿ ويزكيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He purifies them from associating partners with God and from the vices of pre-Islamic ignorance.
rows.anchor: ويطهرهم من الشرك وخبائث الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Book” means the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: ويعلمهم الكتاب ﴾ القرآن ﴿ والحكمة ﴾ السنة أو الفقه في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom can mean the Sunna or understanding of religion.
rows.anchor: السنة أو الفقه في الدين

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muḥammad, they were in manifest error: disbelief and ignorance, with no error greater than theirs.
rows.anchor: من قبل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ لفي ضلال مبين ﴾ كفر و جهالة وإن مخففة من الثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In” is lightened from the emphatic particle; the lām signals it, and the sense is “they were in clear error.”
rows.anchor: وإن مخففة من الثقيلة واللام دليل عليها أي كانوا في ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being presented means being brought for reckoning and questioning, like a ruler reviewing an army to inspect its condition.
rows.anchor: للحساب والسؤال شبه ذلك بعرض السلطان العسكر لتعرف أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing hidden in worldly life remains hidden: neither inner secrets nor any state.
rows.anchor: سريرة وحال كانت تخفى في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufans other than ʿĀṣim read the verb with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالياء كوفي غير عاصم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said people are presented three times on Resurrection Day: the first two are for argument and excuses; at the third, records fly, and the saved take theirs in the right hand and the doomed in the left.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير وأما الثالثة فعندها تطيرا الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought people into existence from earth, using the metaphor of a plant's growth; thus they grew like plants.
rows.anchor: أنشاكم استعير الانبات للانشاء ﴿ نباتا ﴾ فنبتم نباتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God returns people to the earth after death, then brings them out on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: بعد الموت ﴿ ويخرجكم ﴾ يوم القيامة ﴿ إخراجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun emphatically confirms the act of bringing them out.
rows.anchor: أكده بالمصدر أي أي إخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Half of it” is an appositive to “the night”; alternatively, “a little” is excepted from half, meaning pray half the night except a little of that half.
rows.anchor: نصفه ﴾ بدل من الليل والا فليلا استثناء من قوله نصفه تقديره قم نصف الليل إلا قليلا من نصف الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in inquṣ is read with ḍamma by readers other than ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza.
rows.anchor: بضم الواو غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ قليلا ﴾ إلى الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decrease from half is to one third.
rows.anchor: من النصف بضم الواو غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ قليلا ﴾ إلى الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing the half means raising it to two thirds.
rows.anchor: على النصف إلى الثلثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “half” is appositive to “a little,” the options are three: a full half, less than half, or more than half; otherwise the choice is a fixed amount below half or a choice to decrease or increase it.
rows.anchor: والمراد التخيير بين أمرين بين أين يقوم أقل من نصف الليل على البت وبين ان يختار أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Half is called little relative to the whole; in ordinary usage “a little” means less than half, as when all but a little of a thousand is owed, more than half remains due.
rows.anchor: وإنا وصف النصف بالقلة بالنسبة إلى الكل وإلا فاطلاق لفظ القليل ينطلق على ما دون النصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rattala means to articulate and distinguish; the word evokes evenly spaced teeth and well-proportioned speech.
rows.anchor: بين وفصل من الثغر المرتل أي المفلج الأسنان وكلام رتل بالتحريك أي مرتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite deliberately, articulating letters, observing pauses, and fully pronouncing the vowels.
rows.anchor: أو اقرأ على تؤدة بتبيين الحروف وحفظ الوقوف واشباع الحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun intensifies the command and indicates that measured recitation is necessary for the reader.
rows.anchor: هو تأكيد في إيجاب الامر به وانه لا بد منه للقارئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabḥan means the day's extended movement among tasks and concerns, or a long period of free time for sleep and rest.
rows.anchor: تصرفا وتقلبا في مهماتك وشواغلك ففرغ نفسك في الليل لعبادة ربك أو فراغا طويلا لنومك وراحتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persist in remembering God day and night; remembrance includes glorification, declarations of unity and greatness, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, and study.
rows.anchor: ودم على ذكره في الليل والنهار وذكر الله يتناول التسبيح والتهليل والتكبير والصلاة وتلاوة القرآن ودراسة العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul means withdrawing from everything for worship and turning to God alone, hoping for good from Him and no one else.
rows.anchor: انقطع إلى عبادته عن كل شيء والتبتل الانقطاع إلى الله تعالى بتأميل الخير منه دون غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes it as renouncing the world and seeking what is with God.
rows.anchor: وقيل رفض الدنيا وما فيها والتماس ما عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The non-matching verbal noun adds emphasis; it may also be chosen to preserve the verse-end rhyme.
rows.anchor: في اختلاف المصدر زيادة تأكيد أي بتلك الله فتبتل أوجئ به مراعاة لحق الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adnā means less; “nearer” is used metaphorically because shorter distance leaves fewer intervening spaces.
rows.anchor: اقل فاستعير الادنى وهو الأقرب لأن المسافة بين الشيئين إذا دنت قل ما بينهما من الاحياز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in thuluthay is read with ḍamma, except by Hishām.
rows.anchor: بضم اللام سوى هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual and third fractions are accusative for Makkan and Kufan readers, linked to adnā; those reading them genitive link them to “two thirds.”
rows.anchor: منصوبان عطف على أدنى مكي وكوفي ومن جرهما عطف على ثلثي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A group” is coordinated with the pronoun in “you rise”; the coordination needs no emphatic pronoun because intervening words separate them.
rows.anchor: عطف على الضمير في تقوم وجاز بلا توكيد لوجود الفاصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of the Prophet's companions also rose for that amount of the night.
rows.anchor: أي ويقوم ذلك المقدار جماعة من أصحابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can calculate the night and day and know their hours; placing His name first signals His exclusive power to measure them.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقدر على تقدير الليل والنهار ولا يعلم مقادير ساعاتهما إلا الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they stood until their feet swelled, God knew they could not sustain these measures without severe hardship.
rows.anchor: ثم انهم قاموا حتى انتفخت اقدامهم فنزل ﴿ علم أن لن تحصوه ﴾ لن تطيقوا قيامه على هذه المقادير إلا بشدة ومشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's turning toward them means He eased the burden and removed the obligation of night vigil.
rows.anchor: فخفف عليكم واسقط عنكم فرض قيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting what is easy in prayer is obligatory, while reciting it outside prayer is recommended.
rows.anchor: في الصلاة والأمر للوجوب أي وفي غيرها والأمر للندب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means what is available and not difficult for you.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما تيسر ﴾ عليكم ﴿ من القرآن ﴾ روى أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that reciting one hundred verses at night keeps one from being counted among the heedless, and two hundred makes one among the devout.
rows.anchor: روى أبو حنيفة عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال من قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يكتب من الغافلين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some interpret “the Qurʾān” here as prayer, because recitation is one of its pillars; the command is to pray what night prayer is manageable.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد بالقرآن الصلاة لأنه بعض أركانها أي فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم ولم يتعذر من صلاة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command abrogated the first night-prayer command, and the five daily prayers later abrogated it.
rows.anchor: وهذا ناسخ للاول ثم نسخ هذا بالصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The easing is explained by the hardship night vigil would impose on the sick, travelers, and those fighting in God's path.
rows.anchor: ثم بين الحكمة في النسخ وهي تعذر القيام على المرضى والمسافرين والمجاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An” is lightened from the emphatic particle, the sīn replaces its shadda, and its subject is omitted.
rows.anchor: أي أنه مخففة من الثقيلة والسين بدل من تخفيفها وحذف اسمها

words: يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travelers seek God's bounty through trade or the pursuit of knowledge.
rows.anchor: يسافرون ﴿ يبتغون ﴾ حال من ضمير يضربون ﴿ من فضل الله ﴾ رزقه بالتجارة أو طلب العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God places the fighter and the lawful earner on equal footing, because earning lawful provision is jihad.
rows.anchor: سوى بين المجاهد والمكتسب لأن كسب الحلال جهاد

words: يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a patient, reward-seeking merchant who brings goods to a Muslim town and sells at that day's price is counted with the martyrs before God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه ايما رجل جلب شيئا إلى المدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا فباعه بسعر يومه كان عند الله من الشهداء

words: يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that, after death in God's cause, he prefers dying while traveling to earn God's bounty.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما ماخلق الله موته أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن أموت بين شعبتي رجل أضرب في الأرض ابتغى من فضل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recite what is manageable is repeated because the Companions were extremely scrupulous.
rows.anchor: كرر الأمر بالتيسير لشدة احتياطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer to be established is the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة ﴾ المفروضة ﴿ وآتوا الزكاة ﴾ الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zakat to be paid is obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وآتوا الزكاة ﴾ الواجبة ﴿ وأقرضوا الله ﴾ بالنوافل والقرض لغة القطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lending to God means voluntary good works; the root of qarḍ is cutting, as the giver cuts that amount from personal wealth and gives it away.
rows.anchor: بالنوافل والقرض لغة القطع فالمقرض بقطع ذلك القدر من ماله فيدفعه إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loan is attributed to God so donors do not lord it over the poor: the poor assist them in worship, so the donor owes them gratitude rather than claiming a favor.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضافة إلى نفسه لئلا يمن على الفقير فيما يتصدق به عليه وهذا لأن الفقير معاون له في تلك القربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A good loan is given from lawful wealth and with sincerity.
rows.anchor: من الحلال بالاخلاص

words: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people find with God is the reward of their good deeds; the clause answers the conditional.
rows.anchor: أي ثوابه وهو جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is” is an inflectional separator; it is allowed although not between two definite nouns because the comparative resembles a definite noun, being unable to take the article.
rows.anchor: فالمفعول الثاني لتجدوه خيرا وهو فصل وجاز وإن لم يقع بين معرفتين لأن أفعل ما أشبه المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is sent ahead is better than what is left behind, and brings greater, more abundant reward.
rows.anchor: مما خلفتم وتركتم فالمفعول الثاني لتجدوه خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ask forgiveness for sins and for falling short in good works.
rows.anchor: واستغفروا من السيآت والتقصير في الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God conceals the sins and shortcomings of those who sin.
rows.anchor: يستر على أهل الذنب والتقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is merciful by easing matters for those who exert themselves in worship.
rows.anchor: يخفف عن أهل الجهد والتوفير وهو على ما يشاء قدير

none: Surah heading and basmala only; no commentary on the cited verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Make your Lord uniquely great: no one else should loom large in your eyes; say “God is greater” whenever anything other than God confronts you.
rows.anchor: واختص ربك بالتكبير وهو التعظيم أي لا يكبر في عينك غيره وقل عندما يعروك من غير الله أكبر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When this verse came down, the Prophet said “God is greater”; Khadīja rejoiced, recognizing revelation.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه لما نزل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الله أكبر فكبرت خديجة وفرحت وأيقنت أنه الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may refer specifically to the opening takbīr of prayer.
rows.anchor: وقد يحمل على تكبير الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ has a conditional sense: whatever happens, do not neglect magnifying God.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء بمعنى الشرط كانه قيل وما كان فلا تدع تكبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His plotting explains the threat: God hastened poverty and humiliation after his wealth and honor, and will punish his extreme defiance with severe afterlife torment for calling the Qurʾān magic.
rows.anchor: تعليل للوعيد كان الله تعالى عاجله بالفقر والذل بعد الغنى والعز لعناده ويعاقبه في الآخرة بأشد العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thought about what to say concerning the Qurʾān, then devised and prepared his words.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه فكر ماذا يقول في القرآن ﴿ وقدر ﴾ في نفسه ما يقوله وهيأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He was killed” means “he was cursed.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ فقتل ﴾ لعن ﴿ كيف قدر ﴾ تعجيب من تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase expresses amazement at his estimation and plotting.
rows.anchor: تعجيب من تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away from the truth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم أدبر ﴾ عن الحق ﴿ واستكبر ﴾ عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He arrogantly rejected the truth, or acted proudly regarding his own status and speech.
rows.anchor: عنه أو عن مقامه وفي مقاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then he looked” is coordinated with “he thought and plotted”; the curse is parenthetical, and repeated thumma marks the delay between actions.
rows.anchor: ثم نظر عطف على فكر وقدر والدعاء اعتراض بينهما وايراد ثم المعطوفات لبيان أن بين الأفعال المعطوفة تراخيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He called the Qurʾān magic passed down from sorcerers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فقال إن هذا ﴾ ما هذا ﴿ إلا سحر يؤثر ﴾ يروى عن السحرى

rows.speaker: الوليد
rows.claim: Al-Walīd first praised Muḥammad's speech as sweet, beautiful, fruitful, and surpassing human and jinn speech; after Abū Jahl pressured him, he rejected claims that Muḥammad was mad, a soothsayer, poet, or liar, then called the Qurʾān sorcery that divides families and is inherited from Musaylima and Babylonian sorcerers.
rows.anchor: روى أن الوليد قال لبني مخزوم والله لقد سمعت من محمد آنفا كلاما ما هو من كلام الانس ولا من كلام الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ shows that as soon as the accusation occurred to him, he said it without hesitation.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفاء دليل على أن هذه الكلمة لما خطرت بباله نطق بها من غير تلبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell consumes the flesh and spares no bone; alternatively, nothing remains in it without being destroyed, nor can it leave anything intact as it was.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا تبقي ﴾ أي هي لا تبقي لحما ﴿ ولا تذر ﴾ عظما أو تبقي شيئا يبقي فيها إلا أهلكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: S alakakum means “what admitted you into it?”
rows.anchor: أدخلكم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is not itself a report of the believers asking about sinners; it quotes what those questioned report saying to the sinners and what they answered. The narration is elliptical, as Qurʾānic style often is.
rows.anchor: لأن ما سلككم ليس ببيان للتساؤل عنهم وانما هو حكاية قول المسئولين عنهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis treats ʿan as an extra particle.
rows.anchor: وقيل عن زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is admonition, namely the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: عن التذكير وهو العظة أي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turning away” is a circumstantial accusative describing the pronoun, as in “why are you standing?”
rows.anchor: مولين حال من الضمير نحو مالك قائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The asses are wild asses.
rows.anchor: أي حمر الوحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are intensely frightened, as though inciting flight within themselves.
rows.anchor: شديدة النفار كانها تطلب النفار من نفوسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinese and Syrian readers pronounce the fāʾ with fatḥa, giving the sense that something else frightened them.
rows.anchor: وبفتح الفاء مدني وشامي أي استنفرها غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fleeing from qaswara” is a circumstantial clause with qad understood.
rows.anchor: حال وقد معها مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswara can mean archers or a lion; the word derives from qasr, overpowering and domination.
rows.anchor: والقسورة الرماة أو الأسد فعلة من القسر وهو القهر والغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their aversion to the Qurʾān and hearing the reminder is likened to wild asses in flight.
rows.anchor: شبهوا في إعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They want individually delivered sheets that can be unfolded and read.
rows.anchor: قراطيس تنشر وتقرأ وذلك انهم قالوا لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They told the Messenger they would not follow unless each received a heavenly letter addressed by name and commanding belief in him.
rows.anchor: وذلك انهم قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كل واحد منا يكتب من السماء عنوانها من رب العالمين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says they demanded a sheet at each man's head certifying his innocence and safety from Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل قالوا ان كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءته وأمنه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand for a book to read is like the demand in 17:93.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله لن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل عليها كتابا نقرؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” rebukes their demand for individually delivered pages and their proposal of signs.
rows.anchor: ردع لهم عن تلك الإرادة وزجر عن اقتراح الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned away from the reminder because they do not fear the afterlife, not because they were denied the pages they demanded.
rows.anchor: فلذلك اعرضوا عن التذكرة لا لامتناع ايتاء الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” rebukes their turning away from the reminder.
rows.anchor: ردعهم عن اعراضهم عن التذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is a powerful, sufficient reminder.
rows.anchor: وقال ان القرآن تذكرة بليغة كافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever wishes may remember the Qurʾān and not forget it; the benefit returns to that person.
rows.anchor: أي فمن شاء أن يذكره ولا ينساه فعل فإن ذلك عائد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Yes indeed” affirms what the preceding negation denied: God will gather the bones.
rows.anchor: أوجبت ما بعد النفي أي بلى نجمعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Able” is a circumstantial accusative describing the implicit subject of “We gather.”
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير في نجمع أي نجمعها قادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can restore the fingertips exactly as in life, without loss or difference despite their smallness; how much more can He restore the larger bones.
rows.anchor: أصابعه كما كانت في الدنيا بلا نقصان وتفاوت مع صغرها فكيف بكبار العظام
